title: Coming Home from the Hospital: A Checklist for the First Few Days
short_title: Coming home from the hospital: the first few days
description: The first 72 hours home from the hospital carry the highest risk of problems or a trip back to the ER. Here's how to prepare: four questions to ask before discharge, a five-point checklist for the first days at home, the warning signs that mean call right away, and what kind of help works best.
end: Call us before discharge if you can.

parts.head: Coming home from the hospital
parts.sub: How to prepare, and what to watch for
parts.text: Mom's coming home from the hospital. The first few days at home matter more than most families realize. I'm Samantha with Caring Companions in Springfield. Here's how to prepare, and what to watch for.

parts.head: The first 72 hours
parts.sub: The highest risk of problems, or a trip back
parts.text: The first seventy-two hours home from the hospital carry the highest risk of problems, or a trip back to the E R. A little preparation goes a long way.

parts.head: Four questions to ask
parts.text: Before discharge, ask the discharge planner four questions. What follow-up appointments are needed, and when? Which symptoms mean call the doctor, and which mean go to the E R? What changed about the medicines? And is any equipment needed at home, like a walker or a shower chair?

parts.head: One medicine list
parts.sub: New and old together, with a pillbox if it helps
parts.text: Then work through a seventy-two hour checklist. First, put the new and old medicines into one list, with a pillbox if it helps.

parts.head: Book the follow-ups now
parts.sub: Before leaving the hospital, not after
parts.text: Second, schedule the follow-up appointments before leaving the hospital, not after.

parts.head: A clear, safe path
parts.text: Third, clear a safe path at home, especially to the bathroom. Take up loose rugs, and add a nightlight.

parts.head: Someone there at first
parts.text: Fourth, have someone available for the first twenty-four to forty-eight hours, even if it's just to check in.

parts.head: A plan for meals
parts.sub: Not depending on the person who just came home
parts.text: And fifth, plan meals that don't depend on the person who just came home.

parts.head: Call, don't wait
parts.sub: Confusion, fever, worse pain, short of breath, a fall
parts.text: Watch for warning signs. New confusion, a fever, worsening pain, shortness of breath, or a fall. Any of these means call the doctor, or get care right away. Don't wait for the next appointment.

parts.head: Short-term, focused help
parts.sub: For a few weeks while recovery settles
parts.text: Most families in this window need short-term, focused help, not a permanent plan. Help getting around safely, meals, medication reminders, rides to follow-up visits, and someone watching for those warning signs, for a few weeks while recovery settles.

parts.head: Hospital Recovery care
parts.sub: Sometimes starting the same day or the next
parts.text: That's what our Hospital Recovery care is for. Call us before discharge if you can, and we'll talk through your timeline. Once the assessment and care plan are done, care can sometimes start the same day, or the next.
Call us at (417) 234-8494, or visit mo-care.com. I'm Samantha with Caring Companions. Thanks for watching.
